Three dentists, one Bethlehem practice

Meet Dr. Michael Petrillo and the dental team.

Dr. Michael A. Petrillo graduated from the University of Pennsylvania School of Dental Medicine and completed advanced training in surgery and periodontics while serving in the U.S. Air Force. His postgraduate education includes cosmetic dentistry and full-mouth reconstruction.

Dr. Patrick Petrillo and Dr. Bernhard Kabitzke add experience in restorative dentistry, implant restoration, Invisalign, and complete-mouth care. The team uses clinical exams, digital scanning, and 3D imaging when appropriate to explain findings and compare treatment options.

Meet the dentists

Replace missing teeth

Dental implants

A missing tooth can change how you chew, how neighboring teeth meet, and how comfortable you feel when you smile. Dental implants can support a single replacement tooth or be used as part of a larger plan.

3D cone beam imaging helps the dentist examine available bone and nearby structures before recommending treatment. Your visit should also cover alternatives, timing, healing, and the restoration that will be placed above the implant.

Explore dental implants

Clear aligner treatment

Invisalign

Invisalign uses a planned series of clear aligners to move selected teeth over time. An iTero digital scan records the shape and position of your teeth without a traditional putty impression.

The dentist will examine your bite, spacing, crowding, and oral health before deciding whether clear aligners are suitable. The page below explains what to expect from planning, wear, follow-up visits, and retainers.

Explore Invisalign

Before you schedule

Common questions about visiting the practice.

Call the office if your question is about pain, swelling, trauma, or another urgent dental problem.

Is Lehigh Valley Smile Designs accepting new patients?

Yes. New patients can review the forms and insurance information online, then call or use the booking link to request an appointment.

Can I ask about cosmetic and restorative dentistry at the same visit?

Yes. The dentist can first examine the health of your teeth and gums, then explain how treatments such as whitening, veneers, crowns, Invisalign, or implants may relate to one another.

What should I do if a tooth hurts or breaks?

Call the office and describe the pain, swelling, damage, or other symptoms. The team can help determine how quickly you should be examined. Significant swelling, trauma, or signs of infection should not be delayed.

Does the practice offer evening or Saturday appointments?

The office is open until 7:00 PM on Monday and Wednesday and sees patients on the first and third Saturday of the month. Availability varies, so call or check the scheduler for an appointment time.
